title: Creation of an isolate: PA and FL microbes from whole water
author: Aubrey Reed
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.ubcesiw

steps.title: Pre‑filter water and collect filtrate
steps.instruction: Pass whole water through a 20 µm mesh net, collect the <20 µm filtrate in a clean carboy, and retain at least 1 L (≈30 % excess) when filtering 500 mL to ensure enough water for later system flushing.

steps.title: Filter with 3 µm pump and capture samples
steps.instruction: Using the parastolic pump (see Duhaime protocol) equipped with a 3 µm inline filter, pump the pre‑filtered water and collect about 500 mL of the <3 µm filtrate (FL sample) into an Eppendorf tube; then retrieve the 3 µm filter (PA sample), roll it so the dirty side faces outward, and suspend the filter in ~50 µL of 1X PBS in a separate Eppendorf tube.

steps.title: Prepare samples for plating
steps.instruction: Rapidly after collection, vortex and process the PA and FL samples before plating.

substeps.instruction: PA sample: vortex the tube containing the filter for 30 seconds to 1 minute; using sterile forceps, pull the filter slightly out, reseal the cap, and centrifuge the tube for 3 minutes; remove the filter, vortex again and pipette up‑and‑down to resuspend the cell pellet; plate 50 µL of the resuspended sample onto each of four agar types (TSA, BG11, LB, Lake agar).
FL sample: vortex the tube for 30 seconds and plate 50 µL of the sample onto each of the same four agar types (TSA, BG11, LB, Lake agar).

steps.title: Incubate plates and isolate colonies
steps.instruction: Incubate all plates for 2–3 days until a lawn of colonies appears, then select up to five distinct colony morphologies per parent plate and streak each onto a new plate of the same agar type (parent → daughter).

substeps.instruction: Incubate daughter plates for another 2–3 days.
If multiple colonies are present on a daughter plate, split them and plate one of each on separate plates.

steps.title: Restreak colonies for purity
steps.instruction: Perform two additional rounds of streaking (total of three generations) on the isolated colonies until colony purity is confirmed.

substeps.instruction: Second streak: repeat the streak‑out onto fresh plates of the same agar type.
Third streak: repeat once more to ensure a single, pure colony.
Confirm purity by visual inspection of colony morphology after growth.
